newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Study shows EFP improves exchange trade-SFE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Study shows EFP improves exchange trade-SFE.

text.p: A report by U.S. financial markets think tank, the Catalyst Institute, found that 'Exchange for Physicals' (EFP) trading has improved exchange trading, the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) said on Tuesday.

"The findings of this world renowned and highly independent think tank isolate the misconceptions and vested interest views from the practical and factual benefits of EFP trading," said Les Hosking, the SFE's chief executive.

Some sectors of the financial markets have in the past called for the SFE to curtail EFP business citing a perceived drain on trading liquidity, lack of price transparency in EFPs and erosion in trading activity on some fixed interest desks which do not participate in EFP trading, the SFE said.
EFP refers to transactions in which the parties freely negotiate off market a simulataneous futures and physical transaction.

The study, which used the SFE as the benchmark for its analysis, said the prime benefit of an EFP is that the simultaneous transaction of both futures and cash legs ensures more certainty in executing arbitrage deals.
EFPs reduce the exposure to price slippage occuring by executing two separate transactions, one in the futures market and one in the cash market, it said.

The key findings of the study showed that EFPs have increased total trading volume as existing traders make more and larger trades and that market liquidity on SFE's trading floor has not been adversely affected.
It also showed that EFP trading has not increased price volatility and with full price transparency, EFP can and does improve market quality condition on the exchange trading floor.
"The success of EFPs will continue for as long as SFE continues to monitor the effects on transparency in both the on-exchange and EFP markets," the report said.

On the report Hosking said he anticipated that the SFE can encourage further transparency through electronic lodgement of EFPs with the Exchange and the use of quote vendor systems to distribute EFP information to all market participants.

"The report does highlight the continued need for SFE to monitor the effects of EFPs on the price transparency of the markets. To this end, screens have been placed on the SFE trading floor which provide details of EFP trading within one hour of trades being lodged with the Exchange," Hosking said.

"The report demonstrates the value of EFPs provide the on-exchange market, in that it encourages new users of futures markets, adding further volume and liquidity," he added. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
